title: Make pr-head and history checks pending, not failing, on candidate heads
summary: The early PR pushes the job's candidate commit before verification. It carries governed work but no closing records, so `athena check --pr-head` and `--history` refuse it and the first CI run goes red. I read the goal as these checks judging a candidate head as pending (pass with a visible note) and the landing head in full, so both can be required at cutover. The audience is maintainers and CI reviewing Athena PRs.

defaults_applied.how: Fix is in Rust crates (athena-core pr_check.rs, manage.rs / athena-gate history.rs).
Tests for each head shape; cargo test, clippy and fmt --check pass.
Criteria exercise the checks on fixture repos shaped like a candidate push.
Fixes the checks' handling of the candidate head, not just the CI result display.
The pending/fail split is enforced in code with tests, not prose.
Update docs/design/records-history.md section 10 and add a CHANGELOG entry for outside readers.
One focused change to the two checks.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Cause, from reading ci.yml, pr_check.rs and records-history.md: the candidate head changes governed content with no closing records, so classify_commit refuses it under rule 3; the history job fails the same way on the PR head. The failure is not caused by the workflow wiring.

Fix is in the checks, not in skipping CI: a head counts as a candidate only when its content shows it is one (the tip adds governed work and the job's candidate record, with no verification.json or outcome yet). Exact detection rule to be chosen from land.rs/gh/mod.rs open_early_pr during the work.

A candidate head reports 'pending' and exits 0 with a printed note; any other head, including the landing head pushed after verification, is judged as today. Athena alone merges, and only after the landing push, so the final head is fully checked.
Anything that does not match the candidate shape (an unverified human commit, a failed verification, a declared intervention after landing) must still fail.
ci.yml changes only if the checks need extra input (for example a fetch); if it does not change, it is left alone.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-core pr_check`: a test whose head is shaped like the early-PR candidate (governed work plus the job's candidate record, no verification or outcome) makes check_pr_head pass as pending, with the pending state shown in the report.
Run `cargo test --locked`: a test shows the history check on the same candidate-shaped PR head, with main and the records branch present, passes as pending.

Run `cargo test --locked`: heads that are not candidates still fail, naming each offending commit: a governed change with no job records, a head with a failed verification, and a declared intervention after the job landing. The existing pr_check and history_pr_head tests still pass.

Run `cargo test --locked`: a test shows that once closing records (verification and outcome) are pushed on top of the candidate, the landing head is fully judged and passes. A wrong verified fingerprint fails.
`athena check --pr-head` prints a distinct line when a head is judged pending, so a reader of the CI log can tell pending from verified.
docs/design/records-history.md §5.1/§10 and CHANGELOG.md describe the pending treatment of candidate heads and state why the final landing head is still fully checked before it can merge.

out_of_scope: Making pr-head or history required in branch protection (the cutover itself, job 7)
Changing the early PR push or when verification runs
Skipping CI jobs by branch name
The structure-pass follow-ups (stale gh.rs doc paths, run.rs test helper duplication)
Running score-jev --derive on the real records
departures: Slightly above the reference: the change touches two gate checks that both need fixture-repo tests, and the candidate-detection rule is not yet pinned down.
hard_reason: It changes the pre-merge and history checks that gate landing and are to become required checks, so a mistake could let an unverified commit through.
